maria (support): Ticket #C-8241 reporting repeated 503s from hosted inference since ~15:18 UTC. Customer saw timeouts then 503s; reported client error id 0f9b2d.

jordan (oncall): Thanks — can you drop the trace id and any sample request?
maria (support): trace=0f9b2d, sample prompt attached in ticket (shortened). Affected model: redwood-open-1.2 (quantized), region: us-west-2. Error in gateway logs: upstream returned 500 then container restart.
maria (support): Impact: ~3% of requests failing for that customer; started at 15:18, peak 15:24-15:30, still ongoing.
jordan (oncall): I'm seeing many container restarts for the upstream pool serving that model. Restart reason: exit code 137 then SIGSEGV in logs.
deploy-bot: [deployment] service=infer-upstream pool=rw-usw2-quant v=1.2.34 rolled at 2026-03-17T15:05:12Z by ci/canary.
li (eng-runtime): SIGSEGV + OOM pattern suggests a GPU OOM during KV prefetch path or an invalid pointer after a failed allocation. Any model swap or quant change recently?
jordan (oncall): Canary shows quant swap on 1.2.34 earlier today, roll 15:05. We see elevated RSS on process before crash; nvidia-smi shows memory at 100% between restarts.
sam (sre): Could be batch-size regression. Any traffic changes from the customer?
maria (support): Customer says steady qps, no sudden spikes. Their batch size is default (auto-batching).
li (eng-runtime): Grabbed the latest container logs and coredump path: /var/crash/infer-0f9b2d/core. dmesg shows: "Out of memory: Kill process 12345 (infer)" followed by "segfault at 0 ip ..." looks like allocation failed then later segfault during cleanup.
li (eng-runtime): Stack snippet from core (top frames):
```
#0 0x7f9a3c1b in gpukernel::alloc(size_t)
#1 0x7f9a3d22 in kv_cache::prefetch(...)
#2 0x7f9a4f0a in infer::generate_step(...)
#3 0x55aa1b2c in main_loop
```
maria (support): Uploading coredump and logs to the ticket. Also pasting gateway error lines: `upstream error: read ECONNRESET` then `upstream returned 500` repeatedly.
kyle (customer-success): Customer is asking for ETA. We should offer fallback to a smaller model while we triage.
jordan (oncall): Agreed — immediate mitigation: add routing rule to fallback to redwood-open-1.1-small for that customer's route, and temporarily decrease max_batch to 1 for affected pool to avoid bulk allocations.
li (eng-runtime): I'll push a temporary canary that forces max_batch=1 and disables KV prefetching on the quant pool. Also adding a memory cap per container (soft limit) to prevent full GPU saturation.
sam (sre): Rolling those changes now to a single AZ.
deploy-bot: [rollout] config-change pool=rw-usw2-quant max_batch=1 kv_prefetch=off target=canary by jordan at 2026-03-17T15:36:00Z
li (eng-runtime): After patch, one container still crashed but rest stabilized; OOMs dropped from 8/min to 0.5/min in the canary.
maria (support): Customer confirmed errors decreased after 15:40 when you applied fallback. They've accepted fallback for now.
li (eng-runtime): Root cause hypothesis: quant runtime memory regression in 1.2.34 when KV prefetch interacts with certain attention kernel sizes. Repro steps I used: run model redwood-open-1.2 with seq_len=2048, batch=8, kv_prefetch=on, input tokens ~1500, run prefetched warmup twice. Reproduces OOM then segfault within ~30s on our test instance.
jordan (oncall): Good repro. Can we get a bisect to the exact commit?
li (eng-runtime): Starting bisect between v1.2.30 and v1.2.34. Initial suspect is PR #4921 (quant kernel swapping).
sam (sre): For customer-facing fix: continue routing to small model + keep canary config. For longer term: will revert the PR if bisect confirms.
maria (support): Noted for the ticket. I'll prepare postmortem draft and customer summary.
kyle (customer-success): I'll send the customer an update: what changed, expected full restore ETA 4-6h pending bisect.
li (eng-runtime): Next steps: finish bisect (ETA 1.5h), capture heaptrace while reproducing under gdb if needed, run test on non-quant path and quant path with different attention tiling.
jordan (oncall): Also add a monitoring alert to detect memory >90% for pool so we can auto-fallback before 503s.
maria (support): Thanks everyone. I'll mark the ticket as escalated->engineering and include mitigation notes.
